narrationTexts: Let me see the established pattern from an already-migrated file vs. a stale one.
Vendor code is marked do-not-edit; I'll leave that and flag it. Migrating the 12 project files:
Now verifying nothing was missed or mangled:
Let me syntax-check every touched file and confirm the calls actually reach `execute` at runtime:
finalText:
Migration finished. 12 files converted, 32 call sites:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the shape already used in the migrated files (e.g. `accounts/src/repo/user.js`). No test suite exists, so I verified by `node --check` on every file under `packages/` and by running a migrated module against the `lib/db.js` call recorder — all calls land on `execute` with SQL and params intact, including the dynamic `UPDATE ... SET` builder whose spread params survived unchanged.

Two things I deliberately did not change:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** still uses `db.query`. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost. Since `lib/db.js` notes the driver's next major drops `query`, this will break on that upgrade — the fix belongs upstream or in a wrapper, not in the vendored file. Flagging it rather than editing; say the word if you'd like a shim.
- **`cache.query(...)`** across ~20 repo files is a different API on the cache handle, untouched.
